limitations: Historical observations span different measurement/runtime groups; policies see the same frozen feedback, but common-runtime validation remains pending.
Three schedule variants of one Saga family dominate 76.5% of candidate count and 94.6% of available joint score.

The three dominant workloads have identical unordered structural feature vectors. Exact equal indices use fixed ID priority. The two seed1 post-hoc controls show sensitivity, not general performance of a new arm.
LinUCB selection is deterministic; seeds vary local GA and the uniform allocator, not tie priorities.
Cold index calibration is within shared-model and hybrid groups, not between every architecture or later confidence width. H1 also has a recorded floating-point cold near-tie.
Five seeds estimate variability only in this frozen catalogue; no independent generalization or formal significance claim.
Unmeasurable observations are charged to the budget, not labelled score-zero negatives.
Each single-criterion objective also changes GA fitness; cross-objective traces do not isolate the outer bandit alone.
No scenario is measured twice within a run; count-based scores can reward many similar positives rather than distinct defects.
